FINAL_STATES: u2
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, holding_box) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, box_fell) -> u0
(u1, holding_box & at_exit) -> u2
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, else) -> u2
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, holding_box, u1) -> 0.2
(u1, box_fell, u0) -> -0.1
(u1, holding_box & at_exit, u2) -> 1.0
feedback: Several issues: (1) Semantic fidelity: the task requires keeping the box until the exit, but the RM only penalizes a fall (-0.1) and allows eventual exit with box; a subtler issue is that the u1 else self-loop does not track whether the agent is still holding the box while moving toward the exit—states u0/u1 are coarse but acceptable for this task. (2) Reachability/density: the RM is dense only at three transitions; progress toward the exit while holding (u1, holding_box, no at_exit) yields no reward, so no per-step shaping—but 'dense but bounded' is a soft requirement, not fatal. (3) Critical: the transition (u0, holding_box) fires whenever holding_box becomes true, but if box_fell occurs, the RM returns to u0; a re-pickup (holding_box) then re-enters u1 giving reward 0.2 again each time—reward inflation is bounded by 2 falls max, acceptable. (4) Real defect: in u1, the 'else' self-loop silently absorbs the state where the agent holds the box but exits without 'at_exit & holding_box' conjoined properly — that is covered. (5) Actual flaw: at_exit in u0 is absorbed by (u0, else) -> u0 with no reward, which is correct since exiting without the box should pay 0 per the environment—but the RM pays 1.0 at u1->u2 regardless of the environment's conditional requirement; here the task explicitly says keep box until exit, so requiring holding_box at exit is faithful. (6) Most significant: if the agent picks up the box (u1), drops it intentionally without a fall (box stays down, no box_fell event), the RM stays in u1 and can still reach u2 via holding_box & at_exit — correct. But if the agent exits while in u1 WITHOUT holding the box (dropped earlier with no fall), the (u1, else) self-loop fires at the final step and the episode ends in u1, never accepting — the RM then gives no terminal reward even though it is in a non-final state at episode end; the transition (u1, holding_box & at_exit) -> u2 only covers the held case, which matches the task. However the fall-return transition (u1, box_fell) -> u0 loses the information that the agent was near the exit and must re-achieve holding_box — acceptable. Verdict: the machine is mostly faithful but misses reward for silent-fall-avoided exits and offers no shaping; more importantly there is no reward or transition handling the case where the box falls on the SAME step the agent picks it up (pickup then fall due immediately) — this is handled by (u1, box_fell) -> u0, fine. Given the moderate fidelity gaps and lack of dense shaping toward the exit, the artifact is not accepted.
